title: kernel-v1 rule evaluation budget (v1)
description: Versioned source of truth for the numeric constants that bound deterministic rule evaluation (task 28): predicate complexity/depth budgets, immutable list size, scoped exception size, bounded-regex character and timing limits, and temporal-sequence step/window bounds (engine wired in task 29). Tasks reference the schema path rather than hardcoding numbers inline; any number not anchored here is a plan defect. The defaults below are the per-evaluation resource budget the predicate evaluator enforces; an evaluation that would exceed any bound is rejected with a typed error instead of consuming unbounded time or memory.

max_ops_per_evaluation.description: Maximum number of predicate operations (leaf field evaluations) per single condition evaluation (task 28). An evaluation that would exceed this is rejected as too many operations rather than running unbounded.

max_nested_expressions.description: Maximum nesting depth of AND/OR/NOT expressions in a condition (task 28). A deeper condition is rejected as nesting too deep before evaluation.

max_list_items.description: Maximum number of items in a reusable immutable list (task 28). A larger list is rejected so membership evaluation stays bounded.

max_regex_chars.description: Maximum number of characters in a regex pattern (task 28). A longer pattern is rejected as regex too large before compilation.

max_regex_time_ms.description: Maximum wall-clock time in milliseconds for a single regex match call (task 28). A match exceeding this is rejected as regex too slow; the regex engine is linear-time (no backtracking) so this is a defensive bound.

max_exception_items.description: Maximum number of items in a scoped exception value array (task 28). A larger exception is rejected so exception evaluation stays bounded.

max_sequence_steps.description: Maximum number of ordered steps in a temporal sequence (task 28 budget; sequence engine wired in task 29). A sequence with more steps is rejected.

max_sequence_window_seconds.description: Maximum correlation window in seconds for a temporal sequence (task 28 budget; sequence engine wired in task 29). A larger window is rejected.

fixture_min_precision_and_recall.description: Minimum precision and recall a rule pack must achieve on its declared fixture corpus (tasks 30-32). Bench harnesses read this default; the value is NOT hardcoded in the harness scripts.
